def lisLength(arr):
    if not arr:
        return 0
    n = len(arr)
    dp = [1] * n
    for right in range(n):
        for left in range(right):
            if arr[left] < arr[right]:
                if dp[left] + 1 > dp[right]:
                    dp[right] = dp[left] + 1
    return max(dp)

def main():
    # Test case 1: normal case
    arr1 = [10, 22, 9, 33, 21, 50, 41, 60, 80]
    print(lisLength(arr1))
    
    # Test case 2: empty array
    arr2 = []
    print(lisLength(arr2))
    
    # Test case 3: single element
    arr3 = [5]
    print(lisLength(arr3))
    
    # Test case 4: strictly decreasing
    arr4 = [5, 4, 3, 2, 1]
    print(lisLength(arr4))
    
    # Test case 5: all equal
    arr5 = [7, 7, 7, 7]
    print(lisLength(arr5))
    
    # Test case 6: negative numbers
    arr6 = [-5, -4, -3, -2, -1]
    print(lisLength(arr6))
    
    # Test case 7: mixed positive/negative
    arr7 = [3, 4, -1, 0, 6, 2, 3]
    print(lisLength(arr7))

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
